newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK debt vols slide after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK debt vols slide after rate hike.

text.p: Implied volatility of short sterling and gilt options traded on LIFFE recoiled from the gains made earlier in the session, after a rise in British interest rates.

The Bank of England raised interest rates by a quarter-point, taking base rates to 6.75 percent. Most of the market had expected a rise of this magnitude, although the likelihood of a half-point rise had been increasing during the morning session.
"The offers all pulled out of the market, no-one wanted to sell volatility," said a broker at a French house in London. "But not much was done at the higher volatility levels."
September short sterling volatility was nine percent, and December was around 8.9 to 9.2 percent. March 1998 options were 10.6 to 11.0 percent.
"They're all about half a percent lower than this morning's levels," said a trader at a major British brokerage.
A trader said bids as high as 9.8 percent were seen in December, although no-one was interested at those levels.
September short sterling futures were up 0.04 at 92.82 by 1325 GMT, while December was up 0.03 at 92.58.
Gilt option volatility was at six percent for the August series options, 6.2 percent in September, down about 0.2-0.3 percent from earlier in the session, the trader said.
The Bank of England said rapid expansion of domestic demand, led by consumption and the further appreciation of the currency had sharpened the dilemma for policy decisions.
A further rise of a quarter point remains on the cards, and some traders said that the Chancellor's budget last week had not done enough to curb strength in the consumer side of the economy.
Notable trades included September 92.25 puts, where a U.S. house bought 2,000 lots. A major British bank sold 2,000 of the September 92.75 strike puts.
In December, one house bought 3,000 of the 92.00 puts. In March, the 92.50 straddles were traded 200 times at a vol of 11.25 percent. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
